title: Evaluation — FID, CLIP Score, and Human Preference

questions.question: What does mean_vec(vectors) return for a collection of d-dimensional feature vectors?
options: A covariance matrix with d rows and d columns
A scalar equal to the largest feature coordinate
The coordinate-wise arithmetic mean, a vector of length d
One random feature vector chosen from the collection
questions.explanation: The function averages `v[i]` over all vectors independently for each coordinate i.

questions.question: What denominator does covariance use when n>1?
options: It never divides the accumulated outer products
n² for diagonal entries and n for off-diagonal entries
The feature dimension d
n-1 for every covariance entry
questions.explanation: covariance returns each accumulated entry divided by max(n-1,1), using the sample-covariance denominator for n>1.

questions.question: Which terms does fid combine in this implementation?
options: Squared mean distance, covariance traces, and -2 times the trace of sqrt(cov_r @ cov_g)
Only the cosine between one real and one generated vector
The number of human wins divided by the prompt count
The mean absolute pixel error without feature covariances

questions.question: What quantity does clip_like(a, b) return?
options: The Euclidean distance between a and b
The cosine similarity dot(a,b)/(||a||*||b||), with a small denominator floor
The covariance trace of the two embeddings
A binary match that is one only when the vectors are identical
questions.explanation: clip_like computes a normalized dot product and divides by max(na*nb,1e-8).

questions.question: Why can fid(real, gen) be positive even when both sets are sampled from center=0?
options: The code deliberately adds the sample count to every score
FID is defined to be one for identical distributions
Finite sample means and covariances differ, so the estimated distance is biased away from the population value
The inverse routine changes every covariance into a random matrix
questions.explanation: main demonstrates small-N bias: independently sampled finite feature sets do not have exactly equal estimated moments.

questions.question: What does elo_update do when r_a=r_b=1000 and winner='a' with k=32?
options: It leaves both ratings unchanged because the expected score is 0.5
It raises A by 32 and leaves B unchanged
It lowers A by 16 and raises B by 16
It raises A by 16 and lowers B by 16
questions.explanation: At equal ratings expected_a=0.5, so delta=32*(1-0.5)=16; the function adds it to r_a and subtracts it from r_b.
